summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 58 (ipns-signature-verify-coverage) of CipherBox using the GSD workflow — creating PLAN.md files via the plan-phase orchestrator, then executing all 4 plans across 2 waves via execute-phase.
summary.outcome: Phase 58 fully planned (4 plans, 2 waves), executed, verified (7/7 must-haves), and marked complete. All test suites green: cargo core 75, fuse 87, apps/api jest 913/913, sdk-core vitest 243, SDK E2E 89/89. Four advisory code-review findings applied and committed before close.

repo: crates/crypto cannot dev-depend on api-client/core, so cross-language Rust test vectors must live in crates/fuse/tests/ rather than crates/crypto/tests/ to avoid a dependency cycle.
The non-CAS D-09 sequence-validation change class has a known history of breaking SDK E2E (previously caused 48/89 failures), making the full SDK E2E gate load-bearing for 58-02.

TEST_LOGIN_SECRET in the API .env is 'e2e-test-secret-ci-only', which differs from the SDK E2E harness default 'e2e-test-secret-do-not-use-in-production' — a mismatch that silently skips the suite with 401s.
replay.rs in crates/fuse uses bare seq + 1 arithmetic rather than the crate's checked_add convention — flagged as WR-01 in code review and patched in this phase.
Five REQ-IDs (IPNS-05/06, DB-01/02, BYO-08) are absent from the traceability table — pre-existing hygiene debt unrelated to HARD-09.
The commit helper script emits commit_failed as a false negative on success; authoritative verification requires git log, not the helper's exit signal.

code.finding: ciborium dependency is present in the fuse crate — a mid-execution diagnostic claiming it was missing was stale/incorrect.
expectedSequenceNumber guard at line 245 is the CAS 409 conflict check and must be preserved; it is distinct from the D-09 non-CAS sequence gate added in 58-02.

workflow: Sequential subagent execution is safer than parallel worktree execution for security-critical multi-crate phases where correctness outweighs speed.
Spawning verifier and advisory code reviewer in parallel after execution completes is an efficient pattern when their inputs are independent.
An executor subagent overran its plan boundary and executed both 58-02 and 58-03 in a single run — plan boundary enforcement needs explicit prompting or scoping.
When an executor drops mid-task due to a socket error, checking git log and the uncommitted diff before re-spawning avoids duplicating completed work.
Delegating a fiddly infra probe (SDK E2E secret mismatch + correct payload shape) to a focused subagent is more reliable than inline curl experimentation.

friction: 58-01 executor hit an API socket error mid-Task-3, leaving 5 files with uncommitted changes and no SUMMARY — required a manual state assessment and a continuation subagent.
SDK E2E gate silently skipped during 58-02 execution because the running API was compiled from dist with a mismatched TEST_LOGIN_SECRET, producing 401s rather than a clear error.
Probing the test-login endpoint inline with curl failed (both secrets returned 400) because the payload shape was unknown — the investigation had to be delegated.
The 58-02 executor silently continued into 58-03 without stopping at the plan boundary, requiring post-hoc git forensics to understand what actually ran.
commit_failed false-negative from the commit helper caused unnecessary git log investigation after every commit.
open_items: Traceability table is missing 5 REQ-IDs (IPNS-05/06, DB-01/02, BYO-08) — pre-existing hygiene debt, not caused by this phase.
PROJECT.md update was initiated at phase close but its final committed state was not confirmed in the transcript.

RESEARCH.md Open Questions section needed a manual (RESOLVED) marker fix — the plan checker caught this but the planner did not emit it automatically, suggesting a gap in the research agent's output format.
SDK E2E secret alignment between API .env and SDK harness is fragile and undocumented — a shared config or CI env var would prevent silent skips in future phases.
